body.statement:
Under \(\text{ass:multinomial-interior}\), \(\text{ass:multinomial-base-convergence}\), and \(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\), for every rational compact polytope \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 \max_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|\longrightarrow0,
\]
with the maximum interpreted as zero when \(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}=\varnothing\), and
\[
 \left[B'\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}^{-1}B\right]^{-1}\longrightarrow
 \Sigma_0.
\]
body.proof_tex:
Write \(\psi_j(p)=\alpha_j'p+\beta_j\).  The definition of \(e_{n,j}\) and affinity of \(\psi_j\) give the exact identity
\[
 e_{n,j}(u)=\alpha_j'
 \left(\sqrt n[\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}]-Bu\right). \tag{1}
\]
Since \(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\) is finite, Cauchy--Schwarz and (1) imply
\[
 \max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|
 \leq \left(\max_j\|\alpha_j\|_2\right)
 \sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n[\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}]-Bu\right\|_2
 \longrightarrow0
\]
by \(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\).  If the active set is empty the assertion is immediate.

By \(\text{ass:multinomial-base-convergence}\) and \(\min_j(p_0)_j\geq\kappa>0\) from \(\text{ass:multinomial-interior}\), every coordinate of \(p_n(0)\) is eventually at least \(\kappa/2\).  Entrywise inversion of the diagonal matrix is then continuous, so
\[
 B'\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}^{-1}B
 \longrightarrow B'\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1}B=I_0. \tag{2}
\]
For \(x\neq0\), full column rank of \(B\) and positivity of \(p_0\) give
\[
 x'I_0x=\|\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1/2}Bx\|_2^2>0.
\]
Thus \(I_0\) is positive definite.  Matrix inversion is continuous on the positive-definite cone, and (2), together with the definition \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\), proves the covariance convergence.
